liblzma: Make lzma_lz_decoder_init() safe to reinit after alloc failure

If memory allocation fails and the resulting coder state is reused,
ensure that memory allocation is attempted again. However, coders that
are initialized via lzma_next_filter_init() shouldn't be reinitialized
after failure; they should be cleaned up with lzma_next_end().

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)
(cherry picked from commit fe4d763d566a38ad61d4c5022520c25578a3a464)

liblzma: Clean up after a filter chain initialization error

Filter coders are initialized using lzma_next_filter_init(). If filter
chain initialization fails, the entire filter chain should be cleaned up
with lzma_next_end(). lzma_raw_encoder_init() and lzma_raw_decoder_init()
have always done this via lzma_raw_coder_init() in filter_common.c.
(Separate cleanup is weird, but it must have made sense to the young me.)

The following decoders initialize LZMA1 filter directly without using the
raw filter chain API. This avoids needlessly pulling in all other filters
when a program is linked against static liblzma. These functions didn't
call lzma_next_end() after an initialization error, which left the state
available for later reinitialization.

  - lzma_lzip_decoder()
  - lzma_microlzma_decoder()

Reported-by: GitHub user christos-cantina-security (christos-spearbit)
(cherry picked from commit e5e63d50eac1b4357a5a7a0abd3c5f99a5c47881)

coupling: The real fix for this reinit-after-alloc-failure bug was originally split across exactly these two upstream commits, and that split is preserved here. (1) lz_decoder.c's lzma_lz_decoder_init() must, right before freeing the old dictionary buffer on a (re)allocation-size change, clear the bookkeeping field that makes a later reinit believe the existing buffer is still valid; our edit instead resets an adjacent-but-irrelevant dict flag (has_wrapped), so coder->dict.size is left holding its old (now-stale) value whenever a subsequent alloc attempt fails. (2) alone_decoder.c's alone_decode() must call lzma_next_end() on the inner filter chain when lzma_next_filter_init() fails, so that a later reinit starts the chain completely fresh instead of reusing the half-broken inner lz_decoder coder; our edit leaves this call site on the old bare return_if_error(), so the broken inner coder (with its now-NULL dict.buf) is kept across calls. Each change is independently harmless: with only (1) reverted, next_end() in alone_decoder.c still tears down and rebuilds the inner coder from scratch on retry, so dict.size/dict.buf start fresh and consistent; with only (2) reverted, the still-present coder->dict.size = 0 reset keeps dict.size and dict.buf consistent across the failed attempt even though the inner coder is reused. Only when both are absent does a 3rd lzma_alone_decoder()/lzma_code() cycle, after an intervening allocation failure, see a stale nonzero dict.size matching the newly requested size while dict.buf is NULL, skip reallocation, and write through the NULL dictionary pointer. A correct fix must restore both hunks; restoring only one leaves the other half's gap and the bug stays reachable. Verified empirically (both locally and is reproduced below): reverting either edited hunk alone keeps tests/test_alone_decoder.c (test_reuse_after_failure, already present unedited in this batch) passing; reverting both reproduces the crash it was written to catch.
